title: The henselization of a G-ring along an ideal is a G-ring
statement: Let $A$ be a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (in particular Noetherian) and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and let $(A^h,I^h)$, $I^h=IA^h$, be the henselization of the pair $(A,I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Then $A^h$ is a G-ring (in particular Noetherian).

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AH3 (more-algebra-lemma-henselization-pair-G-ring, line 12742; reference Greco, Theorem 5.3 i)) and its proof, invoking Tags 0AGV (henselization-Noetherian-pair), 0AGX (flat-unramified), 0AH1 (filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres), 07PT (check-G-ring-maximal-ideals), and Algebra Tag 07QH (geometrically-regular-over-separable-algebraic)

proof.text: Since $A$ is a G-ring, it is Noetherian. Applying Tag 0AGV to the Noetherian pair $(A,I)$ and its henselization $(A^h,I^h)$ gives that $A^h$ is Noetherian, $I^h=IA^h$, and the canonical map of adic completions $A^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(A^h)^\wedge$ is an isomorphism; it also gives flatness of $A\to A^h$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AH3 proof, first paragraph, invoking Tag 0AGV

proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m^h\subset A^h$ and put $\mathfrak m=(A\to A^h)^{-1}(\mathfrak m^h)$. Because $I^h\subset\mathfrak m^h$ and $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A^h/I^h$ by the henselization pair theorem, $I\subset\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak mA^h_{\mathfrak m^h}=\mathfrak m^hA^h_{\mathfrak m^h}$, and the residue-field map $\kappa(\mathfrak m)\to\kappa(\mathfrak m^h)$ is an isomorphism. Localizing the flat map from Step 1 therefore gives a flat local map of Noetherian local rings $A_{\mathfrak m}\to A^h_{\mathfrak m^h}$ satisfying the hypotheses of Tag 0AGX, so $(A_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(A^h_{\mathfrak m^h})^\wedge$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AH3 proof, first paragraph, invoking Tag 0AGX and the quotient property of Tag 0A02

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset A_{\mathfrak m}$ be a prime and let $\mathfrak q^h\subset A^h_{\mathfrak m^h}$ lie over it. The pair henselization is a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras, and Step 1 says it is Noetherian. Applying Tag 0AH1 to this colimit gives finitely many primes $\mathfrak q_i^h$ of $A^h$ over $\mathfrak q$ and $A^h\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\prod_i\kappa(\mathfrak q_i^h)$, with every extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\subset\kappa(\mathfrak q_i^h)$ separable algebraic; localization at $\mathfrak m^h$ selects the displayed factor containing $\mathfrak q^h$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AH3 proof, middle paragraph, invoking Tag 0AH1

proof.text: Write $C=(A_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak m}}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and $C_h=(A^h_{\mathfrak m^h})^\wedge\otimes_{A^h_{\mathfrak m^h}}\kappa(\mathfrak q^h)$. The completion isomorphism of Step 2 and the product decomposition of Step 3 identify $C$ with the finite product of the factors $(A^h_{\mathfrak m^h})^\wedge\otimes_{A^h_{\mathfrak m^h}}\kappa(\mathfrak q_i^h)$; hence $C_h$ is a direct factor of $C$. Since $A$ is a G-ring, its defining regularity at $\mathfrak m$ says that $C$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, and a direct factor is geometrically regular over that field. The chosen residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\subset\kappa(\mathfrak q^h)$ is separable algebraic by Step 3, so Tag 07QH transfers geometric regularity of $C_h$ from $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ to $\kappa(\mathfrak q^h)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AH3 proof, final paragraphs, invoking Algebra Tag 07QH

proof.text: Steps 2--4 prove geometrically regular formal fibres for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m^h$ of $A^h$ and every prime of $A^h_{\mathfrak m^h}$. Since $A^h$ is Noetherian by Step 1, Tag 07PT, the maximal-ideal criterion for G-rings, implies that $A^h$ is a G-ring.
